## What's new in 0.3.0

### New
- Automatic updates directly from the GitHub repository (Xstrwe/terminyxx): the app checks once a day and silently installs new round versions (vX.Y.0), verified by SHA-256 checksum; applied on next launch.

Security hardening on top of 0.2.5. No critical vulnerabilities were found; the changes below are ordered from high to low severity.

### High
- CI and release workflows now use least-privilege permissions, SHA-pinned actions, build provenance attestations, and optional code signing.
- macOS secrets now use the native Keychain API, with migration from the old items. Previously, any process running as the same user could read stored passwords through `/usr/bin/security`.

### Medium
- Updated `golang.org/x/crypto` to v0.59.0 (GO-2026-6354, GO-2026-6355) and `golang.org/x/text`, and built with Go 1.26.
- SSH connections now use the saved host address from the store, not the address sent by the UI.
- The data folder uses 0700/0600 permissions, plaintext password fallback is gone, and the lock hint is honest about what the lock covers.
- The app lock is now enforced in Go, and OpenURL only allows `http`/`https` links. The recordings folder button works.
- Importing a sync bundle turns off dangerous host flags (agent forwarding, tunnels, jump hosts) and reports replaced hosts.
- Session recordings are listed from the file header and tail, and search streams the file instead of loading it all into memory.

### Low
- Server-controlled input is bounded: read limits, SOCKS connections are capped and cancelled on stop, keyboard-interactive auth is tighter, private-key file permissions are checked, Windows reserved names are filtered, and PTY/window sizes are clamped.
- RDP uses unique temporary `.rdp` files, and Windows credentials are short-lived.
- Plain terminal links now ask for confirmation before opening, and sync file size is limited to 64 MB.
- Frontend dev dependencies (vite, postcss, source-map-js) were updated.

### Notes
- Builds are not Developer ID signed or notarized unless signing secrets are configured in the repository. After installing the macOS app you may need: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Terminyxx.app`
- The x86_64 build was tested on an Intel iMac running macOS 15.
